principle: Keep every genuinely useful free research lane occupied when backlog exists; never create duplicate or artificial work.

phases.name: RUNNER_C_INDEPENDENT_CANDIDATE_DEVELOPMENT
phases.objective: Use one free Windows Runner C for an independent long deterministic candidate-development/readiness workpack; do not duplicate the active Top-4 or Q104:I19 waves.

routing_rules: Skip any workflow that already has an active run.
Do not start the same workflow more than once per phase unless its first attempt failed/cancelled/timed_out and the retry limit permits one retry.
Phase ordering is a preference, not a barrier to independent already-ready work; downstream workflows may self-gate and remain fail-closed.
Existing permanent 10-minute self-hosted and hosted frontier loops remain primary continuous lanes and are not redundantly dispatched here.

Runner C is actively routable for independent reproduction and long deterministic research; it should not be left idle when an independent useful bounded workpack exists. It must not preempt higher-priority work already occupying the slot.
Scientific authority remains unchanged; this scheduler only allocates execution capacity.
Successful source-feasibility workflows are not re-run as filler; only their explicit next-gate workflows may be scheduled.
retarget_reason: The previous Runner-C lease expired. Q120-R2 now has a bounded official CFTC release-exception inventory and Q127-R3 has a distinct bounded Common Crawl metadata route; use the existing Runner-C deterministic readiness/guard workpack while those source probes run on hosted Ubuntu. Q220's multi-GB retry and Q221's repeated 503 route are not restarted.

session_mode.directive: Use Runner C for the existing bounded deterministic orthogonal source/PIT readiness workpack while Q120-R2 and Q127-R3 source metadata probes run separately on hosted Ubuntu. Do not duplicate source downloads or research receipts. Preserve all fail-closed scientific gates and Paper-Only boundaries.
